cross_version_identities.scope: Overlapping (log_n,run,input_digest,protocol-family) identities only; no cross-version timing aggregation

preflight.memory_policy: Linux default first-touch; no explicit NUMA binding/interleave

source_audit.scope: Read-only comparison of archived source bytes, not compiled instruction identity or a performance claim.
source_audit.method: Extract the single fn name occurrence and its balanced brace body from each frozen tar member; remove whitespace only before equality comparison. Comments are retained. The three bodies were inspected to ensure braces inside comments/strings do not alter extraction.
source_audit.limitations: Equal baseline function bodies preserve these source implementations; changed surrounding compilation units can still change compiler inlining/layout or machine code. Bench proof equivalence and real timings remain separately checked.

selection.reason: N26 pair and joint clearly beat basis in this batch; their relative ordering differs between mean and median, so retain both finalists for an independent N30 comparison. Four systems, eight main runs give two balanced rotations; profile is a separate four-run rotation. Same executable, no source changes.

metadata.kernel_scope: reference/lookup/native/tiled/basis/register/split/half/pair/affine/joint select the first aggregation only; native/reuse preserve the v5 kernel; basis/basisreuse retain v6 batched coordinate conversion; register/registerreuse avoid its intermediate zeroing; registerpacked/registerpackedreuse also defer IP message horizontal folds within each packing task; split/splitreuse separate H and continuation accumulation in eight-coordinate loops; half/halfreuse group eight coordinates by sample half; pair/pairreuse unroll paired continuation interpolation with the original consume loop; affine/affinereuse replace split H masks with eight-row GFNI affine maps; joint/jointreuse combine paired interpolation and affine H; split/half/pair/affine/joint retain the v6 Batch conversion and original packing; every mode uses the same mathematical GF256 basis, C projection, weights and IP protocol with hardware fallbacks
